content.value_statement: Choosing the correct mloda plugin pattern requires knowledge of its registry and extension points. This skill guides discovery, implementation, testing, packaging, and publication.
actual_capabilities: Checks the mloda registry guidance before proposing a new plugin.
Explains when to build a FeatureGroup, ComputeFramework, or Extender.
Guides FeatureGroup choices for roots, chains, joins, artifacts, options, and multiple outputs.
Guides ComputeFramework choices for eager, lazy, stateful, conversion, merge, and filter implementations.
Directs testing, package creation, team sharing, and registry publication workflows.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples but does not include executable automation.
It depends on linked mloda documentation for complete implementation details.
It does not verify package availability, compatibility, or current registry contents offline.
It does not replace tests against the selected mloda version and compute framework.

use_cases.title: Create a FeatureGroup
use_cases.description: Choose a FeatureGroup pattern and outline implementation decisions for a new transformation.

use_cases.title: Add an execution backend
use_cases.description: Select the correct ComputeFramework pattern for an eager, lazy, or stateful backend.

use_cases.title: Prepare a community release
use_cases.description: Review testing, packaging, sharing, and registry publication steps for an existing plugin.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a plugin type
prompt_templates.prompt: I need mloda to [goal]. Decide whether I need a FeatureGroup, ComputeFramework, or Extender, and explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Design a FeatureGroup
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a FeatureGroup for [transformation]. Identify inputs, outputs, naming pattern, options, framework needs, and relevant registry guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review a plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my [plugin type] implementation for mloda conventions, dependency handling, feature identity, input forwarding, framework compatibility, and missing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan package publication
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release plan for my mloda plugin covering registry duplication checks, package structure, dependencies, tests, private sharing, and community publication.

output_examples.input: I need a reusable rolling average over an existing feature.
output_examples.output: Use a chained FeatureGroup. Define the naming pattern, forward required options, preserve time ordering, and test supported compute frameworks.

output_examples.input: I want mloda transformations to run on a new lazy backend.
output_examples.output: Implement a ComputeFramework using the stateless lazy pattern. Define conversions, filtering, merging, dependencies, and backend-specific tests.

output_examples.input: My plugin works locally and should be shared publicly.
output_examples.output: Check the registry for duplicates, package from the template, declare optional framework dependencies, add tests, and follow community publication guidance.

best_practices: Check installed and available registry plugins before creating a new implementation.
Choose the smallest plugin type that matches the required extension point.
Test feature behavior, framework compatibility, options, dependencies, and packaging before publication.
anti_patterns: Do not recreate a transformation that already exists in the registry.
Do not use a ComputeFramework for ordinary feature transformation logic.
Do not publish without testing installation and optional dependency combinations.

faq.question: What plugin types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers FeatureGroup transformations, ComputeFramework execution backends, and Extender lifecycle hooks.

faq.question: Does it install mloda plugins?
faq.answer: No. It explains installation choices, but users or agents must run approved package commands.

faq.question: Can it check the live registry?
faq.answer: It points to registry resources. Live checking requires network access and permission to open those resources.

faq.question: Does it generate complete plugin code?
faq.answer: It can guide code creation, but linked guides and project requirements determine the complete implementation.

faq.question: Does it cover plugin testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies relevant testing guides and expected coverage for FeatureGroup and ComputeFramework implementations.

faq.question: Can it help publish a plugin?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines project packaging, private sharing, community publication, and official contribution paths.
